\section{\protect\(p\protect\)\sphinxhyphen{}\protect\(n\protect\) Junctions}
\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:p-n-junctions}}\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:semiconductors-pn-junctions}}\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions::doc}}



\subsection{Introduction to the pn Junction and its Operational Regimes}
\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:introduction-to-the-pn-junction-and-its-operational-regimes}}\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:semiconductors-pn-junctions-regimes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When a \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}type and an \(n\)\sphinxhyphen{}type semiconductor are brought into intimate contact, the immense carrier concentration gradients at the interface drive a transient diffusion process. Mobile electrons and holes annihilate each other at the metallurgical interface, leaving behind uncompensated, fixed dopant ions. This region, stripped of mobile carriers, is known as the \sphinxstylestrong{depletion region}. The fixed charges generate an internal electric field that opposes further diffusion, establishing a balance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Depending on the external voltage \(V_a\) applied across the device, the junction operates in one of three primary regimes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Zero Bias (Thermal Equilibrium, \(V_a = 0\)):} No external voltage is applied. The internal electric field perfectly balances the carrier diffusion gradients. The net current density for both electrons and holes is identically zero (\(J_n = 0, J_p = 0\)).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Forward Bias (\(V_a > 0\)):} A positive potential is applied to the \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}side relative to the \(n\)\sphinxhyphen{}side. This external potential opposes the built\sphinxhyphen{}in field, lowering the electrostatic barrier and narrowing the depletion width. Diffusion forces win over drift, resulting in an exponential injection of minority carriers across the junction.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reverse Bias (\(V_a < 0\)):} A negative potential is applied to the \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}side relative to the \(n\)\sphinxhyphen{}side. The external voltage reinforces the built\sphinxhyphen{}in field, widening the depletion region and increasing the potential barrier. Diffusion drops to zero, and the current is limited to a minute reverse saturation current driven by thermal generation.

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsection{The Depletion Approximation and Shockley Transport}
\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:the-depletion-approximation-and-shockley-transport}}\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:semiconductors-pn-junctions-depletion-approximation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To derive closed\sphinxhyphen{}form analytical expressions for the electrostatics and current\sphinxhyphen{}voltage relations, we employ the \sphinxstylestrong{Depletion Approximation} (also called the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Abrupt Junction Approximation}). This framework assumes that the transition between doping zones is perfectly sharp and that the depletion region is completely devoid of mobile carriers (\(\rho = \text{constant}\) inside the zone, \(\rho = 0\) outside).

\subsubsection{Zero Bias (Thermal Equilibrium)}
\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:zero-bias-thermal-equilibrium}}\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:semiconductors-pn-junctions-depletion-approximation-zero-bias}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By applying the depletion approximation, the net space\sphinxhyphen{}charge density \(\rho(x)\) is treated as piecewise constant:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\rho(x) = \begin{cases} 
  0 & x \lt x_p \\
 -q N_A & x_p \le x < 0 \\
  q N_D & 0 \le x \le x_n \\
  0 & x \gt x_n \ .
\end{cases}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integrating Gauss’ law, \(\partial_x e(x) = \frac{\rho(x)}{\varepsilon}\), with the assumption of electrical neutrality, \(0 = q (N_A x_p + N_D x_n)\), and zero field outside the interface,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}e(x) = \begin{cases}
  0 & x \lt x_p \\
  -\frac{q N_A}{\varepsilon} \left( x - x_p \right) & x_p \le x < 0 \\
   \frac{q N_D}{\varepsilon} \left( x - x_n \right) & 0 \le x \le x_n \\
  0 & x \gt x_n \ .
\end{cases}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integrating the relation between the electric field and the electric potential, \(e(x) = - \partial_x \phi(x)\), with the reference \(\phi(x) = 0\) in the \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk, \(x < x_p\),
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\phi(x) = \begin{cases}
  0 & x \lt x_p \\
  \frac{q N_A}{2 \varepsilon} \left( x - x_p \right)^2 & x_p \le x < 0 \\
  \frac{q N_D}{2 \varepsilon} \left( x - x_n  \right)^2 + \frac{q N_A}{2 \varepsilon} x_p^2 - \frac{q N_D}{2 \varepsilon} x_n^2 & 0 \le x \le x_n \\
  \frac{q}{2 \varepsilon} \left( N_A x_p^2 - N_D x_n^2 \right) =: V_{bi} & x \gt x_n \ .
\end{cases}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Global charge neutrality requires \(-N_A x_p = N_D x_n\), yielding the equilibrium depletion width \(W_0\):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}W_0 = x_p + x_n = \sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon_s V_{bi}}{q} \left( \frac{1}{N_A} + \frac{1}{N_D} \right)}\end{split}
\end{equation*}\subsubsection*{Details}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the continuity of the potential, for \(0 \le x \le x_n\),
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
  \phi(x) 
  & = - \frac{q N_D}{\varepsilon} \left[ \frac{x^2}{2} - x_n x \right] + \phi(0) = \\
  & = - \frac{q N_D}{\varepsilon} \left[ \frac{x^2}{2} - x_n x \right] + \frac{q N_A}{2 \varepsilon} x_p^2 = \\
  & = - \frac{q N_D}{2 \varepsilon} \left( x - x_n  \right)^2 + \frac{q N_A}{2 \varepsilon} x_p^2 + \frac{q N_D}{2 \varepsilon} x_n^2
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thus the potential difference across the depletion region \(V_{bi}\) reads,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
  \phi(x_n) = \frac{q}{2 \varepsilon} \left( N_A x_p^2 + N_D x_n^2 \right) =: V_{bi} \ .
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The width of the depletion region be \(w\) can be written as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
  w 
  & = x_n - x_p = \\ 
  & = x_n \left( 1 + \frac{N_D}{N_A} \right)
    = x_n N_D \left( \frac{1}{N_D} + \frac{1}{N_A} \right) = \\
  & = - x_p \left( \frac{N_A}{N_D} + 1 \right) 
    = - x_p N_A \left( \frac{1}{N_D} + \frac{1}{N_A} \right) \ ,
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
then the potential can be written as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
  V_{bi}
  & = \frac{q}{2 \varepsilon} \left( \frac{N_A^2 x_p^2}{N_A} + \frac{N_D^2 x_n^2}{N_D} \right) = \\
  & = \frac{q}{2 \varepsilon} N_A^2 x_p^2 \left( \frac{1}{N_A} + \frac{1}{N_D} \right) = \\
  & = \frac{q}{2 \varepsilon} w^2 \left( \frac{1}{N_A} + \frac{1}{N_D} \right)^{-1} \ .
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thus the width of the depletion region can be written as a function of the built\sphinxhyphen{}in potential as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}w = \sqrt{\frac{2 \varepsilon V_{bi}}{q} \left( \frac{1}{N_A} + \frac{1}{N_D} \right)} \ .\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{todo} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Deal with some statistical mechanics to show this}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The total voltage drop across the region is the \sphinxstylestrong{built\sphinxhyphen{}in potential} \(V_{bi}\), determined by the bulk doping concentrations and the Law of Mass Action (\(n_0 p_0 = n_i^2\)):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}V_{bi} = V_t \ln\left(\frac{N_A N_D}{n_i^2}\right)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(V_t = \frac{k_B T}{q}\) is the thermal voltage.


\subsubsection{Forward Bias Under Shockley Assumptions}
\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:forward-bias-under-shockley-assumptions}}\label{\detokenize{ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:semiconductors-pn-junctions-depletion-approximation-fwd-bias}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To find the explicit \(I\text{-}V\) relationship, we introduce the \sphinxstylestrong{Shockley Ideal Conditions}:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Low\sphinxhyphen{}level injection (\(n \ll N_A\) in the \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk; \(p \ll N_D\) in the \(n\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No recombination or generation occurs inside the depletion region.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The electric field in the neutral bulk regions is negligible; transport there is purely diffusion\sphinxhyphen{}driven.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Width of the depletion region.}
The applied forward voltage \(V_a\) lowers the barrier, modifying the depletion width to:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}W(V_a) = \sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon_s (V_{bi} - V_a)}{q} \left( \frac{1}{N_A} + \frac{1}{N_D} \right)}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Minority charge injection.} Lowering the barrier causes minority charge injection at the boundaries of the depletion region. Compared to the equilibrium condition with no external voltage,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
  \Delta n(x_p) & = n_{p0} \left[ \exp\left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) - 1 \right] \\
  \Delta p(x_n) & = p_{n0} \left[ \exp\left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) - 1 \right] \\
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Charge transport dynamics.} If Shockley conditions hold, no recombination in the depletion region occurs; recombination occurs in the bulk of \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{} and \(n\)\sphinxhyphen{} sections: in bulk regions, the electric field \(\vec{e}\) is negligible, and thus the current is driven by diffusion only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Governing equation of the holes in the \(n\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk immediately follows from equation \eqref{equation:ch/solid-state/semiconductors-transport-phenomena:eq:semi:num-balance}, with the assumption of no drift current in \eqref{equation:ch/solid-state/semiconductors-transport-phenomena:eq:semi:charge-current-p},
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
  \partial_t \Delta p_n  
  & = - \nabla \cdot \left( \frac{j_{p,diff}}{q} \right) + \Delta ( G - R ) = \\
  & = - \nabla \cdot \left( - D \Delta p_n \nabla n \right) + \Delta ( G - R ) \ ,
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
or in 1\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional problems with constant coefficients
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\partial_t \Delta p_n = D \partial_{xx} \Delta p_n + \Delta ( G - R )\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assuming \sphinxstyleemphasis{steady\sphinxhyphen{}state diffusion equation} (\sphinxstylestrong{todo} \sphinxstyleemphasis{justify this limit}) governs the diffusion of the minority charge carriers in the bulk, and using \sphinxstylestrong{the law of mass action} to write the source term (see box below), the governing equation becomes
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}D_p \Delta p_n'' = \frac{1}{\tau_p} \Delta p_n \ ,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(\tau_p = \frac{1}{k_r n_{n0}}\).
\subsubsection*{Law of mass action for \protect\(\ G - R\protect\)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the \(n\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk region,
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n_{n0} \gg p_{n0}\),

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\Delta n = \Delta p\) if the electrical charge remains zero

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\Delta p_n \gg p_{n0}\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\Delta n_n \ll n_{n0}\)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Thus the source term becomes
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
R - G 
& = k_r p n - k_r p_0 n_0 = \\
& = k_r ( p_{n0} + \Delta p_n ) ( n_{n0} + \Delta n_n ) - k_r p_{n0} n_{n0} = \\
& = k_r ( p_{n0} \Delta n_n + n_{n0} \Delta p_n + \Delta n_n \Delta p_n ) = \\
& \simeq k_r n_{n0} \Delta p_n
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
as:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(G \sim G_0 = R_0\) at equilibrium. \sphinxstylestrong{todo} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Find some time/space to justify all these sentences about equilibrium}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the conditions at the beginning of the box give:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n_{n0} \Delta p_n \gg p_{n0} \Delta n_n\) (because the deltas are equal, and \(n_{n0} \gg p_{n0}\))

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n_{n0} \Delta p_n \gg \Delta p_n \Delta n_n\) (because the deltas are equal, and \(n_{n0} \gg \Delta n_{n}\)

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The differential porblem supplied with proper boundary conditions becomes
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\left\{ \begin{aligned}
  & \frac{\Delta p_n(x)}{\tau_p} = D_p \Delta p''_n(x) \\
  & p(x_n) = p_{n0} \left[  \exp\left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) - 1 \right] \\
  & p(x \rightarrow +\infty) = 0 \\
\end{aligned} \right.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and its solution reads
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\Delta p_n(x) = p_{n0} \left[ \exp \left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) - 1 \right] \exp\left( - \frac{x - x_n}{L_p} \right) \ ,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(L_p = \sqrt{ \tau_p D_p }\) for the holes in the \(n\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk, \(x > x_n\)
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\Delta n_p(x) = n_{p0} \left[ \exp \left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) - 1 \right] \exp\left( \frac{x - x_p}{L_n} \right) \ ,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(L_n = \sqrt{ \tau_n D_n }\) for the electrons in the \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk, \(x < x_p\).%
\begin{footnote}[1]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
The boundary conditions of the diffusion of \(n\) in the \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk are \(n(x \rightarrow -\infty) = 0\), \(n(x_p) = n_{p0} [ \dots ]\).
%
\end{footnote}%
\begin{footnote}[2]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
Usually \(n_0 \ll \Delta n \ll N_A\).
%
\end{footnote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Current under steady conditions.}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Depletion region \(x \in [x_n, x_p]\). Under steady conditions, no charge accumulation occurs along the \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}\(n\) junction and thus the current must be constant. There’s no recombination or generation inside the depletion region \(x \in [x_p, x_n]\), thus the following conditions hold for holes and free electrons
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
     \text{const} & = A J_p(x) = A J_p(x_p) = A J_p(x_n)  \quad \forall x \in [x_p, x_n] \\
     \text{const} & = A J_n(x) = A J_n(x_p) = A J_n(x_n) \ ,
   \end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and thus
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\text{const} = A J(x) \quad \forall x \in [x_p, x_n] \ .\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluating the current at the boundary of the depletion region (in the model, just ouside that, so that the electric field is zero and the current is driven only by diffusion)
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
     I = A J(x)
     & = A J_n(x) + A J_p(x) = \\
     & = A J_n(x_p) + A J_p(x_n) = \\
     & = - A (-q) D_n n_p'(x_p) - A q D_p p_n'(x_n) = \\
     & = A q D_n \frac{1}{L_n} n_{p0} \left[ \exp \left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) - 1 \right] + A q D_p \frac{1}{L_p} p_{n0} \left[ \exp \left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) - 1 \right] = \\
     & = q A \left( \frac{D_n n_{p0}}{L_n} + \frac{D_p p_{n0}}{L_p} \right) \left[ \exp \left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) - 1 \right] \ .
   \end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This equation readily gives the \(V(I)\) relation for an ideal \(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}\(n\) junction,
\begin{equation}\label{equation:ch/solid-state/semiconductors-pn-junctions:eq:semiconductors:pn-junction:iv}
\begin{split} I(V) = I_0 \left[ \exp \left( \frac{V}{V_t} \right) - 1  \right] \ , \end{split}
\end{equation}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with \(I_0 = q A \left( \dots \right) = q A n_i^2 \left( \frac{D_n}{L_n N_A} + \frac{D_p}{L_p N_D} \right)\).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(n\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk, \(x \in [ x_n, +\infty)\). In this region, the electric field is assumed to be negligible, and thus only diffusion drives the current of the charge carriers. For the holes,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
     J_p(x) 
     & = - D_p p'_n(x) = \\
     & = \frac{D_p}{L_p} p_{n0} \exp\left( \frac{V_a}{V_t} \right) \exp \left( - \frac{x-x_n}{L_p} \right) = \\
     & = J_p(x_n) \exp \left( - \frac{x-x_n}{L_p} \right)  \ .
   \end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and thus \(J_n(x) = J - J_p(x)\).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(p\)\sphinxhyphen{}bulk, \(x \in (-\infty, x_p]\)…

\end{itemize}
